answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit jobs, then slash that stake when independent reviewers prove fraud. A ridge of reputation earned through completed work raises the required bond for high-impact tasks, while a quill can record the evidence and pigment mark disputed claims for review. Creating many sybils is no longer free: the attacker must tie up capital in each one and risks losing it, while honest agents build reusable standing.
